thread:
Ivy: Flagging weird output on `garnet-lite` bring-up (Llama->Gemma->Qwen-ish export) int4. Short prompts are fine, but after ~150 tokens we get a flood of <unk> and repeated emoji tokens (like :smile: becomes 0). Anyone seen emoji/NBSP/ZWSP reindexing cause rotary/kv-cache fallout?

Marco: How did you convert the vocab? new `vocabsync` or ad-hoc merge? Any normalization or pruning flags?

Ivy: Used vocabsync v3 with --quant=int4 --prune=true. Ran NFKC. Original vocab head: ['<pad>','<unk>','\u00A0',':smile:',"the",'to',":heart:",'\u200B'] so NBSP at 2 and emoji scattered. After conversion some emoji got compacted and NBSP disappeared. Repro log: 
```
[2026-03-22T18:10:23] INFO step=148 token=189 logp=-3.4
[2026-03-22T18:10:24] INFO step=149 token=0 logp=-14.2
[WARN] repeated token 0 detected; output collapsed
```

Sofia: That looks like reserved-token collision. If NBSP/ZWSP or emoji were removed and indices shifted, anything referencing original ids (kv-cache, rotary precompute) will be wrong. Did the converter emit a dense remap table or did you apply in-place index shift?

Ivy: It did an in-place shift. I assumed runtime would handle sparse ids. Also we use a micro-optimisation that packs tokens into bytes assuming contiguous id range for the quant layout; that could cause collisions if ids are sparse.

Marco: Two likely failure modes: 1) sparse->dense packing assumption in quant causes remapped ids to alias to 0 or compact into pad slot, 2) runtime rotary fallback uses token_id as a cheap hash for phase precompute in one path. If token ids change mid-sequence, rotary phase misaligns and you get sudden logp collapse.

Ivy: Re-ran with vocabsync --prune=false and --emit-remap-file; forced preserve for control/emoji tokens. Validation perplexities: baseline=12.2, converted-prune=25.7, converted-preserve=12.4. Repeats gone.

Sofia: Good. Let's add a converter lint that refuses to prune any token classified as invisible or emoji in the top K indices (e.g., first 256). Also require the remap file be produced and validated by runtime on model load. Runtime should error if it detects remap->packed aliasing.

Marco: Add an eval: sliding-window mean logp across tokens 1..512 with seeds [1,2,3], fail if mean-delta >0.3 vs baseline. Also add a short test that takes a representative emoji-heavy prompt (from tests/emoji_long.txt) and asserts no token id 0 spikes.

Ivy: I'll PR: vocabsync flag --preserve-reserved-classes, emit remap JSON, and add lint + emoji_long test + doc blurb in onboarding/vocabs.md about quant packing assumptions.

ci-bot: build 2110 started for vocabsync on branch onboard/garnet-preserve

ops-bot: scheduled canary run on dedicated-us-west-2 pool for 12h, task id r-3321

Sofia: Also file a runtime note: change the rotary precompute fast-path to use position index not token id; if that requires remap support, make it explicit. We should avoid token-id-based heuristics.

Ivy: Yep. I'll include a tiny unit that asserts precompute uses positions.

Marco: One more: quant packers often assume max_id < 2^n contiguous. Add a converter sanity that writes dense_id_range and runtime should accept sparse remap or fail early with a helpful message.

Ivy: Opening PR now, will tag Marco/Sofia for review. Thanks!
summary: Onboard/garnet-lite: pruning removed NBSP/emoji caused id shifts -> quant packing & rotary precompute assumptions broke; fixed by preserving reserved tokens, emitting remap, and adding lints/tests
